Forestar sold 11,629 lots to Horton in FY2026 for US$1,291.5m (86% of its lots sold), about 23% of Horton's finished-lot purchases.

Forestar is separately capitalised (US$1.3bn liquidity, 6.7% net debt to capital) and its debt is not guaranteed by Horton. A Forestar stockholder derivative suit (Mississippi PERS v. D.R. Horton, Del. Ch., filed 2025-04-29) challenges lot-sale transactions between the two companies. Forestar's Executive Chairman Donald J. Tomnitz retired 2026-10-31; CEO Anthony W. Oxley became Executive Chairman and CEO on 2026-11-01. Verification 2026-11-19: Forestar FY2026 10-K states revenues from lot sales to D.R. The January 2024 deal also gave the seller $16,620 plus 2% of proceeds per home sold (https://therealdeal.com/miami/2024/01/22/kolter-pays-74m-for-491-homesites-at-avenir-in-palm-beach-gardens/). Counterparty: EB5AN (EB-5 regional center and fund manager)

Source: EB5AN offering page: Spring Haven (Loan with Repayment Guaranty)

Arrangement: Development company of Peachtree Building Group principal Doug Cotter. Eastwood's CFO says it remains an active land development partner for the Atlanta division after the May 2026 acquisition, i.e. a continuing source of developed lots.

Source: Elementix company profile: Eastwood Homes (public-records aggregator)
Research note: Derived by the aggregator from recorded documents; purpose inferred from the entity name and activity, not confirmed by the company.

Arrangement: BWS is a Brookfield Corporation affiliate. It holds land under financing arrangements that Brookfield Residential buys back as lots, and from 2025 a land option agreement under which Brookfield Residential pays option maintenance fees and deposits for the right to buy lots. In the first nine months of 2026 it paid $49.2M for lots and $16.1M for land bought from BWS.

Research note: In the 2025 Annual Report, 2025 lot takedowns from BWS were $83.1M (2024: $60.3M) and the liability fell from $117.3M (Dec 2024) to $53.7M (Dec 2025); the land option agreement with BWS was entered in 2025. amount_usd_m is the outstanding liability at Q3 2026, not the program size, which is not disclosed. Lot count not disclosed.

Counterparty: Homebuilder Finance (Brookfield Residential US Land Holdings LLC, II LLC and III)
Arrangement: Brookfield-affiliated landbanking vehicles that Brookfield Residential invests in, so here it is on the land-banker side. It holds 49.0%, 22.2% and 26.5% interests, carried at fair value as 'Homebuilder Finance Investments' ($63.6M at 30 Sep 2026; $78.0M at Dec 2025). It also lends to Homebuilder Finance: up to $50M at SOFR+2.0-2.75%, with $9.0M outstanding at Dec 2025 (Dec 2024: $56.8M under a $125M line).
Source: Brookfield Residential Q3 2026 Interim Report (MD&A and notes, approved 2026-10-28)
Research note: Ownership percentages and loan terms come from the 2025 Annual Report, Note 3 and receivables note (https://edge.sitecorecloud.io/097dc95ddd47-brookfieldr25d6-prodb938-e22e/media/project/brp/brp/global/modules/financials-and-disclosures/annual-and-quarterly-reports/2025-annual-report.pdf). The builders these vehicles land-bank for are not disclosed.

Counterparty: Third-party land and lot option sellers (not named)
Arrangement: Off-balance-sheet land and lot option contracts. At 30 Sep 2026 Brookfield Residential had $62M of mostly non-refundable deposits and entitlement costs and a $283M remaining exercise price, up from $21M and $180M at Dec 2025. A further $114.1M of deposits backs land purchase obligations with $1.3B committed (Dec 2025: $637.4M).
Source: Brookfield Residential Q3 2026 Interim Report (MD&A and notes, approved 2026-10-28)
Research note: Counterparties not disclosed. The remaining exercise price is split into $47.2M on options included in inventory and $235.4M on options held in receivables. The steep rise in purchase commitments ($637M to $1.3B in 2026) is the main sign of new land demand.

Counterparty: Daiwa House USA Holdings Inc. (parent; wholly owned by Daiwa House Industry Co., Ltd.)

Source: Daiwa House: Notice Concerning Change of Specified Subsidiary in the United States

No third-party land banker or lot-option financier is named for CastleRock in any source opened. 2026-11-19 check: description previously said this equity funds CastleRock land; the source says only that the holding company was set up to facilitate financing, so that wording was removed.

Arrangement: The group's in-house land company. It acquires, entitles and develops communities and delivers finished lots to Legend Homes and to the rental affiliate SimplyHome; it reports more than 25,000 lots and more than 100 communities developed since 1989 in Houston, Dallas-Fort Worth, San Antonio and Bryan-College Station. Source: Camillo Companies Names Sean Mulroony President of Academy Development (company press release)
Research note: Terms between the affiliates (lot pricing, takedown schedules, who holds title) are not public. The 25,000 figure is lots developed over the company's life, not lots held today. The 100-plus communities figure is from https://www.camillocompanies.com/our-companies (opened 2026-11-19), not the Mulroony release, which states only the 25,000 lots.

Counterparty: SimplyHome (formerly Camillo Properties; Camillo Companies affiliate)
Arrangement: Build-to-rent sister company that designs, builds, leases and keeps single-family rental homes on lots from the same Academy Development pipeline; some communities are split between SimplyHome rentals and Legend for-sale homes. It reports more than 10,800 rental homes built in 115-plus communities as of August 2026.
Source: Camillo Companies - Our Companies page
Research note: Relevant because it competes with Legend for the affiliate's lots and may account for part of reported unit volume. A search-result snippet of Builder's 2026 firm profile for Legend Homes (https://www.builderonline.com/?p=117360, page returned 403 so not opened) shows 165 single-family build-to-rent units alongside 1,457 closings in 2025; whether those rentals are inside or on top of the closings figure is not confirmed. The split-community point is from the 2023 HousingWire feature.

Arrangement: Third-party master developer of Bluestem, a 356-acre community in Brookshire (Waller County, Houston area), where Legend Homes took an initial section of 116 lots and opened for sales in July 2024. Shows that Legend buys lots from outside developers as well as from its affiliate.
Source: Legend Homes Announces Debut in Bluestem, a New Waller County Community (company press release)
Research note: Lot purchase terms (takedown schedule, option versus bulk purchase) are not disclosed.

Counterparty: TerraLane Communities (build-to-rent division of IHP Capital Partners)
Arrangement: Owner-client, not a land banker. TerraLane bought the 22-acre Queen Creek site itself and hired Hancock as general contractor for the 218-unit TerraLane at Hudson Station, the sixth community the two firms have done together. Shows the pattern: the client's capital holds the land.
Source: TerraLane Buys Land, Breaks Ground on 218-Unit Build-to-Rent Project Near Phoenix (REBusinessOnline)
Research note: IHP Capital Partners is a residential land and homebuilding investor, so it is itself a capital source in Domain's world. Hancock's projects page lists six TerraLane communities (Goodyear x2, Phoenix x2, Surprise, Queen Creek).

Counterparty: Blueprint Capital (Seattle; principal Dan Duffus, also of SolTrust)
Arrangement: Owner-client, not a land banker. Blueprint entities own the Canopy at Sundance (Buckeye), Canopy at Cottonwood (Casa Grande) and Sonoran Row (Phoenix) rental communities; Hancock acted as both developer and general contractor on the Canopy projects.

Arrangement: Owner-client, not a land banker. Hancock was brought in as general contractor to recover six delayed 'Bungalows' build-to-rent projects totalling 1,247 units in Buckeye, Prescott Valley (two), Casa Grande, Goodyear and Phoenix.
Source: Hancock Builders: Projects page

Arrangement: Owner-client, not a land banker. Family investment group for which Hancock has delivered three Vlux-branded rental communities (Peoria, Queen Creek, Phoenix).
Source: Hancock Builders: Projects page
Research note: Date is the page-as-of date.

Arrangement: Owner-client, not a land banker. Canadian-rooted developer for which Hancock built rental communities in the Arcadia area of Phoenix (Ara and Lyra) and Avondale (Cottages at McDowell). A WestStone vice president credits Hancock with the land purchases as well as the construction.
Source: Hancock Builders: Projects page

Arrangement: Owner-client, not a land banker. Real estate investment firm for which Hancock built The Montgomery at Rancho Mercado in Surprise.
Source: Hancock Builders: Projects page
Research note: A testimonial for the same project is signed by Tony Koeijmans of McCarthy Companies. Date is the page-as-of date.

Arrangement: Owner-client, not a land banker. Developer for which Hancock built The Douglas at Goodyear Airport Commons in Goodyear.
Source: Hancock Builders: Projects page
Research note: Date is the page-as-of date.

Arrangement: Hayden bought RYN Built's lot supply and RYN agreed to provide single-family lots in multiple projects across the Tri-Cities and Spokane markets, while RYN kept doing land development and apartments. A builder-to-builder lot-supply deal, not a land bank.
Source: Hayden Homes Acquires RYN Built Homes Lot Supply (company release)

Counterparty: All Pro Capital / All Pro Funding V, LLC
Arrangement: Investor debt fund managed by All Pro Capital (founded by Brian Bahr) that lends to National Builder Group to build homes and develop land. Loans are secured by first or second deeds of trust at 75% of value or less, and The Challenger Group, Inc. guarantees the fund. This is secured lending, not a lot-option land bank.
Source: All Pro Capital: Current Offerings (All Pro Funding V)
Research note: Amount outstanding is not public. The fund's 2021 SEC Form D set a maximum offering of $100 million; the website currently markets $10 million as available. First sale 2021-02-18 per Form D.

Arrangement: Definitive agreement for a newly created land fund of up to $150M to fund development of raw land into finished lots for UHG's markets. Sponsor/manager and pricing not disclosed.
Source: UHG Q1 2024 earnings release (8-K Ex. 99.1, filed 2024-05-10)
Research note: Announced with Q1 2024 results. Whether this fund is the same vehicle as 'GSH Land Fund, LLC' (named in the 2026 information statement) is not disclosed; no Form D was found on EDGAR under either name.

Arrangement: Described in the merger information statement as the third-party land bank working on UHG's behalf. A December 2025 proposal from Nieri-affiliated developers asked UHG to direct the fund to sell common-area acreage and road access at the Halton Oaks community to one of those developers.
Source: UHG DEFM14C information statement (filed 2026-04-10)
Research note: Sponsor, size and lot count not disclosed. In September 2025 Stanley Martin's proposal also required third-party consents under UHG's 'land banking agreements', which confirms more than one such contract existed. The counterparties to those agreements are not named.

Counterparty: Unnamed third-party land banker (finished-lot sale and repurchase option)
Arrangement: Starting in Q1 2024, UHG sold finished lots to a land banker and took options to buy them back. This is accounted for as a financing: the lots stay on the balance sheet as real estate inventory not owned, and the land banker funds about 80% of their carrying value. Q1 2024 proceeds were $14.2M, and inventory not owned was $17.8M at 2024-03-31.
Source: UHG Q1 2024 Form 10-Q (filed 2024-05-10)
Research note: UHG's maximum exposure was $1.9M at 2024-12-31 and $0.2M at 2025-12-31 (FY2025 10-K Note 2, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1830188/000183018826000009/R9.htm), so the program had nearly run off. In 2024 UHG also paid closing costs for a related party to move land to one of its land banking partners (FY2025 10-K Note 9).

Counterparty: PC Entities (Land to Lots, LLC; PC Land Development Co., LLC; Pennington Development, LLC)
Arrangement: Land developers affiliated with controlling stockholder and former Executive Chairman Michael Nieri, with lot option contracts that historically supplied a large share of UHG's developed lots. The February 2026 'PC Property Agreements' sped up UHG's purchase of finished lots and raw land at Camellia Park, Palomino Oaks and Southbridge, added a new raw-land purchase at Winter Farms, and included the Halton Oaks acreage sale. Source: UHG DEFM14C information statement (filed 2026-04-10)
Research note: Entity names and the PC Property Agreements are from the DEFM14C. Nieri's restrictive covenants were narrowed in his February 2026 waiver, so these entities may stay active as South Carolina lot developers outside Stanley Martin.

Source: UHG FY2025 10-K Note 2, Variable Interest Entities (XBRL R9)
Research note: amount_usd_m is the remaining aggregate purchase price under option contracts, not deposits.

Source: Daiwa House news release: Notice Regarding Purchase of Equity Interests of Trumark Companies LLC (16 Jan 2020)
Research note: Sellers were family trusts of Michael Maples and Gregg Nelson (50% each before the deal); expected transfer date 1 Feb 2020. The same release says Trumark had been procuring project funds from institutional investors (not named) and would shift to using its own funds. Amounts of capital contributed since are not disclosed. The Orange County Business Journal (23 Mar 2026) still describes the stake as 60%; no later change was found.

Counterparty: Master-plan land sellers (not named in the releases)
Arrangement: Trumark buys lots inside third-party master plans as well as stand-alone sites. Announced in 2025 and 2026: 37 more lots at Sterling Ranch (Littleton, CO), described as acquired; 85 homes at Andara at the Great Park (Irvine) and 90 at Sunflower at Rienda in Rancho Mission Viejo, described as secured; and plans for 195 homes at The Trails in Bishop Ranch (San Ramon), where the release does not say whether the land is owned or under contract. No release names sellers, prices or any option or phased-takedown structure.
Source: Trumark Homes Expanding Southern California Footprint in 2026 (27 Jan 2026)
Research note: Lot count is the sum of the four master-plan deals named (37 + 85 + 90 + 195). Sterling Ranch and Bishop Ranch details are in Trumark's releases of 12 Dec 2025 and 27 Aug 2026 (see capital_events). Whether any of these are rolling-option takedowns is not public. Verifier 2026-11-19: description corrected; the 27 Aug 2026 Bishop Ranch release announces plans to build and does not say the site was acquired or secured (earlier text said all four were acquired or secured). The cited 27 Jan 2026 source states only the Great Park and Rienda counts.

Checker 2026-11-19: neither cited source ties Wildleaf to North River Ranch; the 2024 profile states the partnership only in general terms.

Arrangement: Master developer of Kingston in Estero (more than 7,700 acres, approved for up to 10,000 homes). Neal Communities is one of three builders, with Pulte and Lennar, in the 3,625-home Kingston South neighbourhood, where it is building six models and selling villas and single-family homes; grand opening was 17 October 2026.
Source: Neal Communities release: Kingston Community in Estero Features Four Quality Builders
Research note: Neal's lot count and whether it bought its Kingston South land outright or takes lots down over time are not disclosed. Florida Weekly (October 2026) describes Kingston as developed by 'Cameratta Companies and Neal Communities'; Gulfshore Business describes Neal as a participating Phase 1 builder.

Arrangement: National nonprofit loan fund (CDFI) in Silver Spring, MD, serving NeighborWorks member organisations. Lends for acquisition of vacant land or existing property (typically up to $10 to 15 million), predevelopment (up to $3 million, can revolve), construction including single-family (up to $20 million), mini-perm, permanent and enterprise loans. This is the network's nearest equivalent to land finance, at nonprofit pricing.
Source: NeighborWorks Capital website (home and Loan Capital pages)
Research note: Amount is the permanent equity capital NeighborWorks America has put into NeighborWorks Capital (over $43 million, plus operating support), per its site; it says it has provided over $600 million of funding in total (undated). Operates independently but 'in strategic alignment' with NeighborWorks America. Leaders per its staff page: Jim Peffley, Chief Executive Officer (since 2022); Nancy Wagner-Hislip, Executive Vice President running lending, credit and portfolio (named July 2026); Matt Glatting, Chief Financial Officer; Ben Greenberg, Chief Lending & Customer Engagement Officer; Beth O'Leary, Chief Risk Officer. Not a land banker and no lot-option structure.

Arrangement: National nonprofit lender (CDFI) in Decatur, GA, that describes itself as financing exclusively NeighborWorks America organisations. Products include lines of credit for early-stage costs, acquisition loans for vacant land and existing properties, single-family and multifamily construction, bridge, permanent, forward commitments and a warehouse line for nonprofit mortgage lenders; up to 95% loan-to-value.
Source: Community Housing Capital website (loan products, home and team pages)
Research note: Site totals (undated): $1.3 billion of capital deployed, $4.1 billion total development, 25,374 homes, 44 states. Leadership change: Cindy Holler, President and CEO, is retiring; Dana Chestnut, EVP/Chief Lending Officer, becomes President and CEO on 2027-01-01. Arif Rizvi is EVP/Chief Financial Officer. NeighborWorks America funds it with grants from its appropriation (described as an affiliated 'Capital Corporation' in the budget justification). Not a land banker and no lot-option structure.
